## Decisions
- **`LocalSeconds` on `ResolvedGenerator`, not reusing `Progress`** → atmospherics are rate-driven (a longer clip drifts further, not slower), unlike title scroll which is duration-relative. Kept both fields since title-family generators still need `Progress`.
- **Descriptor-driven `GeneratorDescriptor.Parameters`/`Colors` instead of one bespoke Inspector section per generator** → mirrors `EffectDescriptor`'s existing pattern; means the six atmospherics needed zero custom Inspector code beyond a single generic `BuildGeneratorSection` branch, and any future generator registered the same way gets a UI for free.
- **Two-layer particle field (near + far, decorrelated via a jitter offset) instead of one lattice** → single lattice read as an obvious uniform grid to visual reviewers; two layers at different scale/rate gives depth and breaks the regularity.
- **Per-particle spawn-gate bias for Embers/Sparks source falloff, not a per-pixel alpha multiply** → alpha-multiply approach was invisible once the accumulated field saturated (dense presets hid the gradient entirely); gating which particles spawn at all (keyed to position along flow direction) is what actually thins the field visibly.
- **Cloud "ground bias" (`Falloff` param) also anisotropically warps the noise domain (squash X, stretch Y)**, not just a vertical density multiply → a pure multiply pooled the same billow shapes into a corner; the domain warp is what turns billows into full-width horizontal fog layers.
- **Premultiplied-alpha test reads raw `SKBitmap.Bytes`, not `GetPixel`** → `GetPixel` unpremultiplies on the way out in SkiaSharp, which silently hides the exact defect class being tested for.
- **`TempDump.cs` test class** is a deliberate throwaway, gated behind an env var so it's inert in CI/normal runs — not meant to ship; flagged in Unfinished Tasks for removal.
